response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-19
CLINICAL INDICATION: On treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer. Increasing shortness of breath over one week.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. M. Castellanos (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-09-02. The prior report states lungs clear and does not mention a line. On the prior image, mildly coarse right lower zone markings, a left hilum fuller and denser than the right, and a left-sided central venous catheter are seen (see Findings).
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Differences from prior: the prior is displayed with higher contrast and the current is softer and flatter. The prior is mildly rotated and the current is not rotated. These differences limit confident comparison of subtle hilar density, hilar size, mediastinal contour and small nodules.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- None flagged as time-sensitive. Priority review order: left hilar change (F1), left hilar ring lucency (F6), right lower zone markings (F5, F8), cardiac silhouette (F7). Triage urgency is high: SpO2 91 percent with one week of worsening breathlessness in metastatic cancer makes the unresolved left hilar question more pressing to review.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea is central with the expected slight rightward deviation at the aortic arch. No central airway narrowing is seen at this resolution. Lung volumes are large. No focal consolidation, collapse or discrete mass in any zone. Mildly coarse markings in the right lower zone, similar on the prior (seen on one read only; overlying soft tissue may contribute). Mildly prominent bronchovascular markings at the right base without focal consolidation (one read only; some haze may be overlying breast soft tissue). Vascular markings reach the chest wall on both sides. A tiny density projects over the right medial upper zone near the anterior first rib end on the prior only; indeterminate (see CAN'T DETERMINE).
- Mediastinum / hila: Aortic knuckle is prominent, consistent with an unfolded aorta, and is similar to the prior. Upper mediastinum is not widened. Right hilum is unremarkable. Left hilum: INDETERMINATE, the two reads disagreed. One read found the left hilum fuller and denser on the prior than on the current, which would suggest it is smaller now. The other read found the contour and bulk similar on both films and attributed the denser prior appearance to higher image contrast. The current left hilum is not bulky. A small ring shadow, possibly a bronchus seen end-on, projects over it on the current study. The differences in contrast and rotation between the studies could explain the apparent change.
- Pleura: Both costophrenic angles are sharp on both studies. No pleural line and no visible pleural thickening. Diaphragm and upper abdomen: the left dome is level with or slightly higher than the right on both studies, with a gas-filled stomach and bowel beneath it and no gas under the right dome. Change in the gas distension under the left dome is INDETERMINATE, the two reads disagreed (one read stable, one read decreased on the current). The left base is partly overlapped by gas-filled bowel.
- Heart: Heart is not enlarged on this PA film and its borders are defined. One read described the silhouette as at the upper limit of normal for a PA film. Size and contour are similar to the prior.
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or destructive rib lesion is seen at this resolution. Degenerative change at both shoulders and the lower cervical spine. No soft tissue gas. Fine bone detail is limited on both images. Line: a left-sided central venous catheter enters from the left lateral chest or axillary region and crosses the midline, with its tip projecting over the right paramediastinal region at the expected level of the superior vena cava. Course and tip position match the prior. No new device. The insertion site is not on the film.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: No definite interval change established. Left hilar change is indeterminate (reads disagreed; one read suggests smaller on the current, one read suggests stable). Change in gas distension under the left dome is indeterminate (reads disagreed). A tiny right medial upper zone density is seen on the prior only and is not clearly seen on the lower-contrast current film; indeterminate.
- Unchanged: Aortic knuckle contour and mediastinal width. Left-sided central venous catheter course and tip position. Heart size and contour (similar). Coarse right lower zone markings (seen on one read; stable). Relative height of the domes. No new consolidation, pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or new lung nodule or mass compared with the prior.

RECIST 1.1: Not computed. No confirmed measurements. (RECIST input: not computed on radiographs.)

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the left hilum truly smaller on the current study than on the prior? | Reason: The prior has higher contrast and mild rotation, and both can make one hilum look larger and denser. A frontal film alone does not separate vessel from node or mass. | Recommend: CT chest with contrast, and review of the source images in PACS.
- Is the tiny density over the right medial upper zone on the prior a lung nodule or first rib costochondral calcification? | Reason: The density is well under the size at which X-ray separates a nodule from bone or a vessel end-on. It is not clearly seen on the lower-contrast current film. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. CT chest if it persists on review.
- Is there opacity behind the heart or at the left base? | Reason: The relatively high left dome and gas-filled bowel overlap the left base and retrocardiac region on a frontal film alone. | Recommend: Lateral view or CT chest.
- Is there a focal bone lesion in the ribs, shoulders or spine? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, so fine bone detail is not assessable. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS.
- Is the left hilar fullness vascular (pulmonary artery) or nodal? | Reason: A frontal film alone cannot separate vessel from lymph node, and the difference in image contrast between the two studies limits judgment of subtle density change. | Recommend: Correlate with any previous cross-sectional imaging. If none is available, contrast-enhanced CT chest.
- Is the small ring lucency over the left hilum on the current study a bronchus seen end-on or a small cavitary or cystic focus? | Reason: The structure is small, overlaps hilar vessels, and is seen on a downsampled frontal image only. It is less conspicuous on the higher-contrast prior. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS. Lateral view or CT chest if it persists.
- Does the asymmetry of the breast shadows reflect previous left breast surgery, or positioning? | Reason: Soft-tissue contours are partly outside the field and faint at this resolution. The asymmetry makes the right lower zone look hazier than the left on both studies. | Recommend: Correlate with surgical history. Do not read the right lower zone haze as lung opacity without that correlation.
- What is the exact catheter tip position relative to the cavoatrial junction, and what type of line is it? | Reason: The carina and the right atrial junction are not sharply defined on these images, and the insertion site and any reservoir lie outside the field. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing. Correlate with the line insertion record.
- Are there small nodules in the retrocardiac region, at the apices or behind the diaphragm domes? | Reason: Only a single frontal view of each study is available. These areas are hidden by overlap, and small nodules cannot be separated from vessels seen end-on or from rib ends. | Recommend: Lateral view, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Is there a subtle rib, spine or shoulder lesion? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, and fine bone detail such as cortex, pedicles and small lucent lesions is not reliably shown. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS on bone settings.

IMPRESSION:
1. Left hilum: change since the prior is indeterminate. The two blind reads disagreed (one suggests smaller on the current, one suggests stable), and differences in contrast and rotation between the studies may account for the appearance. Vascular versus nodal fullness cannot be separated on a frontal film. Not resolved; needs radiologist review and measurement.
2. Small ring lucency over the left hilum on the current study, possibly a bronchus seen end-on (seen on one read, described as stable). A small cavitary or cystic focus is not excluded on this film.
3. Mildly coarse right lower zone markings, similar to the prior, with no focal consolidation (one read). Overlying soft tissue may contribute.
4. Mildly prominent bronchovascular markings at the right base without focal consolidation, similar to the prior (one read). Haze may reflect breast asymmetry; do not read it as lung opacity without correlation with surgical history.
5. Heart not enlarged on this PA film, similar to the prior. One read described the silhouette as at the upper limit of normal.
6. No new consolidation, pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or new lung nodule or mass compared with the prior. This single frontal film does not show a cause for the breathlessness, and the left hilar question remains unresolved.
7. Other items: change in gas distension under the left dome is indeterminate (reads disagreed). Left-sided central venous catheter is unchanged, with its tip projecting over the expected superior vena cava; exact tip position and line type cannot be determined. Aortic knuckle prominence is stable. A tiny right medial upper zone density on the prior only is indeterminate.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- CT chest with contrast for the left hilar question. The interval is not specified in the findings and is left for the attending to set.
- Review of the source images in PACS, including windowing for the catheter tip and bone settings.
- Lateral view or CT chest for the retrocardiac and left base region and for possible small nodules. The interval is not specified in the findings and is left for the attending to set.
- Correlate with prior cross-sectional imaging, surgical history and the line insertion record.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
